articleTitle: DNN-SVM Automatic ECG Signals Heartbeat Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: An electrocardiogram (ECG) is a graph of the electrical activity of the heart. It can assess the health of the cardiovascular system. It also contains information that allows distinguishing heart disease, which is the leading cause of death worldwide. In order to provide the correct diagnosis, researchers developed techniques for the automatic classification of heart diseases. We developed two models: Deep Neural Network DNN and Support Vector Machine SVM algorithms for an automatic heartbeat classification for high-accuracy disease diagnosis. With DNNs, we achieve 97.45<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> correct classification rates and 90.33 % with SVMs. Normal, unknown, ventricular ectopic, supra-ventricular ectopic, and fusion beats were the five categories of ECG signals. Furthermore, in terms of accuracy, this method outperforms others.

articleTitle: Optimal Pricing of Multi Virtual Power Plants Based on Stackelberg Game and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: With the rapid development of distributed energy, virtual power plants (VPPs) need to integrate distributed energy and electricity market transactions. There is a game competition relationship between different virtual power plants.In order to maximize the profit of the control center and minimize the operation cost of the virtual power plant, this paper establishes a master-slave game model of multiple virtual power plants and control centers, and uses genetic algorithm (GA) to find the equilibrium solution. In the process of iteratively searching for the optimal solution, the objective function of the control center in each round of game is used as the fitness value of the genetic algorithm, and then carries out the selection, crossover and mutation of individuals in the feasible solution population. Finally, the optimal transaction price can be obtained quickly. The results obtained by the example demonstrate that the proposed model reduces the operating cost of the virtual power plant and inproves the revenue of the control center, which verifies the effectiveness of the method and achieves a win-win situation for both the virtual power plant and the control center.

articleTitle: Energy Management Trade-off: Virtual Optimization of Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: As the attention on hybrid electric vehicle concepts has raised, the complexity of the systems and the number of requirements for simulation and calibration have increased significantly. Hence, virtual methods have been introduced to frontload calibration and validation efforts, while reducing cost and increasing robustness and maturity. However, the applicability of these simulation-based methods depends on the hybrid powertrain and vehicle simulation, the optimization approach, and the objective assessment of the powertrain operating strategy, which defines the cost function to achieve satisfactory calibration optimization results. Therefore, in this paper, a virtual calibration methodology for energy management of HEV vehicles is presented, by employing objective assessment within a closed-loop optimization of a hybrid powertrain co-simulation workflow that contains comprehensive vehicle, powertrain, and HCU models. By using the proposed method, the trade-off between efficiency and driveability optimum calibrations was investigated.

articleTitle: Production-Ready Deep Learning Model Optimization for Anomaly Detection in Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Anomaly detection in photovoltaic systems using deep learning models can help further automatize classification tasks and support the operator in decision making. However, the performance of pretrained deep learning models decreases in production owing to the difference between training and production data (domain shift). This performance gap can lead to serious problems when monitoring photovoltaic (PV) farms. To this end, this study proposes an approach to adapt new instances to fit the constraints of the input layer of the pretrained model by image segmentation using Niblack thresholding, padding, and resizing. In addition, the localization of single panels was calculated using metadata. Moreover, a retraining cycle was proposed to include new instances in the training process to fine-tune the models and adapt the weights to the images taken during production. The proposed algorithm extracted 81% of the panels from the images fed into it. However, the pretrained model, which was used to classify the segmented images to test its performance, did not perform well. This indicates the importance of the retraining process for optimizing the model for production.

articleTitle: BAC TTS Corpus: Rich Arabic Database for Speech Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Recorded Speech Corpus (RSC) is one of the key elements of corpus-based synthesis. Sentence length and corpus size are additional factors that affect the Speech Synthesis (SS) sound quality, along with the quality and coverage of the Speech Corpus (SC) in each unit and its representations. This study suggests a method for creating SS systems based on Arabic corpora. This fact covers the investigation of the standards used to create a corpus-based SS. More than 5 million words have been gathered in an initial corpus in order to accomplish our goal. To this end, a variety of sources are gathered, including newspapers and the Shamela Arab Library. To design the sentences for the SC, the initial corpus was analyzed using phonemes and the occurrence of words to identify all high frequency phonemes and words. A 202-sentence supervised phonetically balanced SC with 6174 phonemes has been created. The findings demonstrate that the unit coverage in the corpus has an actual influence on the perceived SS quality.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Medical Assistant Robot for Hospitals: An Approach with IoT-Powered Physiological Monitoring and Patient Interaction
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, an Arduino based medical assistant robot is proposed which monitors primary health conditions (temperature, pulse rate) of the patients and connects health experts remotely via app-based IP camera. The design and development of a medical assistant robot for the disabled patients and those in need are the main idea of this project. In hospitals and health centers, the main goal of such a robot is to minimize human involvement while maintaining cleanliness, sanitation, and help critical patients during emergency situations such as quarantines for infectious disease like Covid 19. This proposed design has extra features such as medication reminder system, an automatic hand sanitizer, and a patient monitoring system powered by the IoT (body temperature, pulse rate). The architecture of this project is based on many electrical components like micro-controller, LCD display, infrared sensor, pulse sensor, motor driver, IP camera, water pump etc. This device is powered by 12V battery which senses temperature, calculates heartbeat, and pulses by using a BPM sensor. The main objective of this work is to increase safety for the doctors as well as patients to reduce the spread of infection by using remote communication via IP camera during quarantine time. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Development of a Power Transformer for a Fast Charging Station
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This article discusses charging stations for battery electric vehicles including cars, forklifts, motorcycles, scooters, railcars, watercraft, buses, trucks, etc. The different options of the block diagram of the fast-charging station are shown depending on the location of the output voltage and current control link. Weight and dimensions of used power transformer are important criterion when selecting the block diagram. For this reason, equations for calculating the weight and dimensions of a power transformer are obtained depending on the block scheme, variation range of the output voltage and primary and secondary winding schemes. The results of the development of the prototype with the output voltage 48 V and the output power 7.7 kW are presented. The developed prototype of the fast-charging station showed that the weight of the power transformer compared with calculated value is lower by 11 %, and the volume is lower by 7 % which is acceptable for engineering experience. This article is of interest for technical specialists who develop both charging stations for battery electric vehicles and adjustable DC/DC converters for different electrical engineering systems.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Multicarrier NOMA for 5G NR System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Multiple Access (MA) techniques in wireless systems are either Orthogonal MA (OMA) or Nonorthogonal MA (NOMA). OMA suffers from less spectral efficiency (SE), while NOMA is struck by inter-user interference. Due to the diversity of applications in Fifth Generation (5G) and Beyond 5G (B5G) communications, the trade-off between complexity and performance in Multicarrier NOMA (MC-NOMA) takes a lot of attention. In this paper, a combination technique between orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) and NOMA employing 5G new radio (NR) flexible numerology to achieve an enhancement in the MC-NOMA performance is proposed. One base station (BS) and three downlink users are considered. The results show a considerable enhancement in achievable sum rate and users' data rates as compared with OMA and NOMA. Although the bit error rate (BER) of the proposed system is higher than that of OMA, it provides a reasonable enhancement as compared with NOMA. A mathematical model of BER performance for a two-user scenario is expressed too. The model showed its correctness in a comparison between system analysis and simulation. The proposed system reaches a bit rate of 400 Mbps at a 5dB signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) value, whereas OMA and NOMA provide about 240 Mbps at a 5dB SNR value when they tested over 32MHz carrier bandwidth.

articleTitle: Digital Twin for Oyster Mushroom Cultivation Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The agricultural industry has excellent potential to grow because of the vast opportunities and demands. However, despite the significant potential in agriculture, especially mushroom cultivation, there are still some problems, such as a gap between yields and market demand, because mushroom cultivators cannot produce optimal mushroom production in quality and quantity. Proper and effective cultivation processes must be carried out to produce quality oyster mushroom products in large quantities. Implementing the digital twin concept by utilizing Internet of Things and Machine Learning technology will have many good impacts to make it easier for mushroom cultivators to monitor oyster mushroom cultivation. The digital twin concept will focus on characteristics so it can represent physical objects as closely as possible. IoT will playa massive role in providing data in real-time through sensors so that things that cannot be seen physically can be known based on their data and machine learning will support the virtual modeling process so that monitoring data for mushroom growth will be available in real time according to their respective characteristics. Implementing the digital twin concept in the mushroom cultivation monitoring system requires five stages: creation, communication, aggregation, analysis, and insight. Based on the research, the digital twin concept has a huge opportunity to optimize the mushroom cultivation process because it will help mushroom cultivators know the mushroom's environmental and physical conditions in real time. Besides that, implementing digital twins will help predict environmental and mushroom conditions, harvest time estimates, treatment recommendations on each of the different mushroom characteristics, and other informative insights.

articleTitle: An Efficient 1D Autoencoder-Based Approach for R-Peaks Detection in Electrocardiogram Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Electrocardiogram (ECG) signal which is composition of multiple segments such as P-wave, QRS complex and T-wave plays a crucial role in evaluating human heart cardiac diagnosis. For an analysis of cardiac diagnosis, it is required that clinicians scan the ECG signal for R-peaks (the highest peak of the QRS complex) detection, which relies on their expertise and takes enormous time. In order to provide more realistic treatment of cardiovascular diseases in the ECG signal with noises and different characteristics, computer-based R-peaks detection approaches have been actively developed in the research article for many years and generally compose of two major operations; preprocessing and decision. Contrary to previous approaches which require high computational costs and complexity, appropriate initial parameters, a novel CNN based approach is presented for R-peaks detection in this paper. Both qualitative and quantitative analysis are performed in the real ECG signal taken from typical MIT-BIH arrhythmia database. In order to validate the success of the recommended approach, total 18 different R-peaks detection approaches reported in the literature are compared by utilizing performance evaluation metrics. Average values of sensitivity, positive predictivity, error rate, accuracy and f-score are computed as 99,96%, 99,95%, 0,09%, 99,90% and 99,95% respectively, which are the best values among well-established studies for R-peaks detection. It is demonstrated with qualitative and quantitative results that better performance is achieved by our suggested approach.

articleTitle: Hand Gesture Recognition through Reflected Infrared Light Wave Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Gesture recognition is an important application of human-computer interaction (HCI) which can enable computerized systems to perform various tasks based on hand gestures performed remotely. In this study, we present a non-contact gesture recognition method using only incoherent light wave signals reflected from a human subject. In comparison to existing radar, light shadow, sound and camera-based sensing systems, this technology uses a low-cost ubiquitous light source (e.g., infrared LED) to send light towards the subject's hand performing gestures and the reflected light is collected by a light sensor (e.g., photo detector). This light wave sensing system recognizes different gestures from the variations of the received light intensity within a 20–35 cm range. The hand gesture recognition results demonstrate up to 96 % accuracy on average. The developed system can be utilized in numerous HCI applications as a safe, low-cost and non-contact gesture recognition technology.

articleTitle: A Critical Review of Spatial Domain Multiple Image Encryption Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: At a time when image sharing is becoming more frequent and widespread, it is a necessity to ensure the security of shared images. Image encryption methods can protect shared images against attackers who may seek to possess images. Instead of encryption methods that can encrypt only one image, the number of multiple-image encryption algorithms that can provide security for increasing image sharing is increasing in the literature. This paper presents a critical review of the recently published multiple-image encryption algorithms. The inadequacies encountered in spatial-domain multiple-image encryption algorithms are emphasized in this work. Possible solutions and new approaches to these shortcomings are presented.

articleTitle: Current Control of Grid-Connected Simplified Split-Source Converters (S3I) for Single Phase Photovoltaic Microinverter Application
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents design of grid-connected single phase simplified split source inverter and effective grid current control strategy for photovoltaic (PV) microinverter application. The operation of principle of the split-source inverter is discussed and how the proposed current control method is applied to the related system is explained in detail. The simulation is carried out by using Powersim (PSIM) software environment to demonstrate the operating of the proposed system. The proposed microinverter system includes the PV module and simplified split source inverter. The grid current is adjusted to a value that corresponds to maximum power operating point of the PV module and this power is transferred to grid in a microinverter system. The maximum power of PV module is obtained using perturb and observe (P&O) method and unipolar sinusoidal pulse width modulation (SPWM) is used for simplified split source power converter. Various simulation tests have been performed on the proposed micro inverter system at various and constant irradiation values. The simulation results show that grid current control strategy is implemented on simplified split source inverter for the single-stage PV -grid-connected power generation competently, producing constant DC-link voltage. Reduction of number of switches, high voltage boosting gain and no need for additional DC-DC converters are features of high efficiency simplified split source inverter.

Author Keywords: grid connected simplified split source inverter

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a Piezoelectric Fan System for Advanced Cooling Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Electronic components are under thermal stress due to the heat generated by the power losses during their normal operation. In order to prevent damage and guarantee long term reliability while performing their functions properly, their temperature should be maintained below a specified limit all the time. The importance of this research is to ensure that electronic components stay at the specified temperature based on ambient conditions with component-based cooling. The aim of this study is to perform mechanical analysis and design of the piezoelectric fan that provides component-based cooling for small areas, and to analyze the electronic driver used to control the airflow provided by the cooler. This work included the mechanical analysis and design of a heat sink for keeping the FPGA material at a sufficient temperature on an add-on card inside the enclosure, considering the ambient parameters inside the enclosure. Piezoelectric material was preferred to provide movement in the cooler design. Consistent with the mechanical analysis of piezoelectric material, the electronic control to provide the required motion was analyzed. The advantages of analog and digital circuits were compared for electronic control and evaluated the suitability of generating the required signals with digital circuits. The required signal was produced by making simulations on the control with H-Bridge structure with the SPWM method. As a result of the mechanical analysis, the type of heatsink that provides the most effective cooling, the surface area of the heatsink in contact with the air, and the airflow velocity were determined. A modal analysis for the electronically generated signal concluded that the required pulsation should be a sine wave at first mode frequency of piezoelectric fan with no other frequencies at which the piezoelectric material is stimulated.

articleTitle: Classification of high frequency transient events buried in low frequency sampled PMU data
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents a deep-learning based method for the classification of transient events of the power system using the data collected by a standard Phasor Measurement Unit (PMU). Although transient power system events are high-frequency variations of the voltages and currents, it leaves a trace in the PMU time-series data, which are collected at relatively much lower-frequencies. The main motivation of this study is to use low-frequency data recorded by PMU devices, widely used in the industry, for the classification of transient events, which would normally require the use of high-cost power quality analyzers. In the proposed method, PMU data are converted into 2D data by Gramian Angular Field (GAF) image transformation method to increase the classification performance. Then, the GAF matrices corresponding to PMU time-series data are classified by a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) based deep learning method. Transient event data used in this research work includes different numbers of frequency and angle time series of three different events, Line Trip, Generation Trip and Load Shedding, obtained from the Frequency Disturbance Recorders (FDR) developed at Virginia Tech. FDRs are connected to the FNET/GridEye network hosted by the University of Tennessee. Classification performances on the three power system events show that using only the frequency data gives the best performance results compared to that using angle only and both frequency and angle. Impact of the training data amount is examined for all cases and future work is proposed. Although there are similar studies in the literature, contribution of this research work is revealing the effect of PMU data type and size of training set in detail.

articleTitle: A Triband Multifunction Frequency Selective Surface
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a Triband Multifunction Frequency Selective Surface (TMFSS) is proposed. There are four number of p-i-n diodes used in TMFSS unit cell which are biased on parallel biasing principle. Between 1~2.0 volts are required only to feed the diodes in a layer of full board. Three bands can be selected for transmission and reflection in multiple ways along with polarization control. The operating bands work at 2.0 GHz, 3.9 GHz and 5.0/5.47 GHz frequencies. Multiple codes are assigned on the basis of biasing to p-i-n diodes and working principle of TMFSS in terms of different behavior. The codes 0000 and 1111 meet transmission through TMFSS at 3.9 GHz and 5/5.47 GHz to dual polarizations of plane wave, respectively. Meanwhile, both states reflect frequencies other than their selected transparent windows. The codes 0011 and 1100 supply polarization asymmetry besides switching between two bands residing at 3.9 GHz and 5.47 GHz frequencies. The codes 1011 and 1101 provide polarization inversion and switching at 2.0 GHz. However, these codes provide dual polarization transparency at about 5/5.47 GHz with little drift in center frequency. The code 0001 is transparent for TE wave at 2.0 GHz and 5 GHz. This code reflects the 3.9 GHz band at which the TMFSS is transparent to TM wave. The code 1000 makes the TMSSS transparent for TM wave at 2.0 GHz and 5.0 GHz. This code reflects the TM wave at 3.9 GHz band at which the TMFSS is transparent to the TE wave. articleTitle: Simulation of NO2 Gas Sensor Based on Multistrip Couplers Surface Acoustic Wave Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Surface Acoustic Wave (SAW) gas sensor for nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) detection utilizing the Multistrip coupler (MSC) is numerically investigated. A model for SAW-MSC based on LiNbO3 as a piezoelectric substrate and employing the copper phthalocyanine (CuPc) as a sensing layer for the NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas sensor is explored. The sensor signal originates from surface conductivity changes induced by the adsorbed NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. This variation in conductivity leads to a changing coupling efficiency of the multistrip coupler and, thus, to variations in the insertion loss (IL) of the device under the adsorption influence of the NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas concentration. The number of electrodes has been optimized. Then, the impact of the NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas concentration, up to 3000 ppb, on the change in the velocity is explored. The results reveal an almost linear behavior of the IL versus the gas concentration. The obtained results are found to agree well with the previous experimental results.

articleTitle: Examination of Effects of Shipboard Conducting Structures on Electrical Characteristics of HF Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The aim of this study is to examine the effect of the warship's conductive structures (such as guard rails and the main mast) on the electromagnetic (EM) characteristics of high frequency (HF) communication antennas. Towards this aim, electromagnetic analyses of the HF antennas are performed in order to determine how the existence of guard rails and different physical dimensions of the main mast affect the electromagnetic characteristics of these antennas in terms of return loss levels, electromagnetic coupling levels and far field radiation patterns. These analyses are performed by using time domain solver of Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Studio Suite<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>.

articleTitle: Re-Configurable Power Divider Based on Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Future Millimeter Wave (mmWave) band communication systems are predicted to be involved in different and diverse fields. These systems will be smart with high speed that enable the emergence of fundamental and advanced services. In order to realize these systems we need the use of reconfigurable microwave components implemented based on modern guiding structures. Power dividers are considered one of the essential components for the feeding antenna system. In this paper, Re-configurable Printed Ridge Gap Waveguide (RPRGW) is deployed to implement a power divider. The simulated results show a wide bandwidth of 16 % at 38.5 GHz. These results demonstrate the merit of using this technology to implement various microwave components suitable for smart communication systems.

articleTitle: Implementation and Performance Analysis of Multi Channel ARINC 429 Controller on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Communication interface is one of the most important part for an electronic equipment in an avionic vehicle especially commercial (civil) ones. Data buses like Arinc-429 and Arinc-664 are solves this part. In this paper, Ethernet based multi-channel Arinc-429 controller is implemented and analyzed on Xilinx FPGAs. A fully functional digital design for Arinc-429 data bus controller is developed. It converts Arinc-429 bus to Ethernet bus. Avionics LRU manufacturers who need to develop a multi-channel Arinc-429 converter can benefit from this design approach and methodology. Xilinx Artix-7 Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) device is used for the implementation. Arty A7 development board and HI-3593 ARINC Dual Receiver/Single Transmitter Demo Board was used in the experiment. The design controls 6 receiver channels and 3 transmit channels. Each receiver channel has dedicated buffer to store bus data. The hole design uses 9279 slice LUTs, 7233 slice registers, 4 RAMB36s, 92 RAMB18s and 46 IOB. So, a low cost and portable- (generic) implementation is achieved.

articleTitle: Passive Architecture and Renewable Energy's Integration
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The Algerian Saharan cities with a variety enormous resources remain the poor relative of conceptions adapted to developed cities, our problem seems topical as it refers us to recurring questions in several areas such as urban planning, architecture, and renewable energy. To understand the relationship between architecture and renewable energy, it is important to study construction techniques and understand the specific environmental context in which each building fits. This paper aims to question the integration of new techniques for energy exploration with traditional architecture in a context of sustainable environment for an original case of a house in the ksar of Taghit. To address the scientific demonstration inherent in this relationship through a corpus studied beforehand through an analysis of the environmental data of the Taghit-ksar of the wilaya of Béchar, it is useful to highlight their natural resources and propose a model of low-consumption housing, taking into account natural resources and architectural options.

articleTitle: TiO2/SiO2-Filled Composite with Spatial Permittivity Distribution for Application in FGM Spacer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This research paper presents a comparative study of non-linear permittivity distribution models for spacers with functionally graded materials (FGM). FGM is an effective solution for controlling the electric field in the Triple Junction (TJ) area between conductors, spacers and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SF}_6$</tex> gas. An increase in the electric field strength often occurs at the junction of the conductor with the spacer. This electric field concentration can be reduced by using the spatial distribution of permittivity of the U-FGM type. To obtain the FGM spacer model, the desired spacers relative permittivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}})$</tex> distribution model has been designed to be between 3.5 and 7.5. The results of the analysis show that spatial permittivity distribution model have been able to reduce the electric field concentration by 27% in the Triple Junction - High Voltage (TJ-HV) region from 11.596 kV/cm to 8.458 kV/cm. Furthermore, this study made FGM specimens using TiO2/SiO2 - filled composite can obtain the desired permittivity distribution of the U-FGM model. When the filler loading weight is 30% of the total weight of the epoxy resin material, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_\mathrm{r}$</tex> value is between 3.7 to 6.8. While the composite filler loading has 40% of the total weight of the epoxy resin material, the measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}$</tex> is 4.1 to 12.5.

articleTitle: Beamforming Network for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the design, analysis, and implementation of switched beamforming network operating at 5.2 GHz for 5G applications. It is intended to launch four beams. The Butler matrix feeding network is presented to electronically switch the beam in the desired direction. This work achieves a good approach to alleviate the problem of cross-over implementation and fabrication. A Four-element array of printed antennas is designed and fabricated. The network and array are implemented on Rogers RT/duroid 5880 substrate with a relative permittivity of 2.2 and a thickness of 1.04 mm. The different scattering parameters are simulated using both ADS and CST which conduct good agreement between the simulated and measured results.

articleTitle: Comparison of Quantum-Digital to Thermal Method in AC Voltage Measurements
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The latest generation of high-performance digital converters (digitizers) requires more functional and accurate systems for their testing than existing thermal converter-based alternating voltage metrology can provide. The latest research shows that this problem can be solved by applying Josephson quantum voltage standards. This was the reason that TUBİTAK UME, the National Metrology Institute of Turkey, launched a program that includes; defining the digitizer calibration methodology using Josephson's voltage standards, expanding the measurement range by constructing and applying new voltage dividers, evaluating the measurement uncertainty as well as validating the new method by comparing it with the existing thermal method which is presented in this paper. First, the digitizer was calibrated using the new digital-quantum approach and later compared with the thermal method in measuring AC voltage. The results of the comparison show that these two techniques give very close results in the considered range, promising that the proposed quantum-digital method with a possible extension of the measurement range can be the basis for new traceability of AC voltage.

articleTitle: Magnetic Shielding Simulation for a Low Noise Atomic Comagnetometer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Design and simulation studies of a low-noise magnetic shielding unit were carried out for atomic comagnetometer applications. The aim of this study is to find the optimum solution with the highest attenuation rate by characterizing the performances of magnetic shielding units with different designs. Simulations of four different designs were carried out. As a result, it has been determined that with a four-layer magnetic shielding, attenuation rates greater than 106 can be obtained and the magnetic field of 50μT can be reduced below 1pT.

articleTitle: Improved Kidney Outlining in Ultrasound Images by Combining Deep Learning Semantic Segmentation with Conventional Active Contour
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Computer-aided diagnosis systems are used to process kidney ultrasound images with the goal of providing the clinicians with objective, computer-based analyses to improve the diagnosis accuracy. A crucial requirement to develop these systems is to accurately outline the kidney in ultrasound images. The majority of the computer-based methods that are proposed for outlining the kidney in ultrasound images are based on conventional segmentation approaches, such as active contour algorithms. Recently, deep learning semantic segmentation models have been employed to outline the kidney in ultrasound images. However, limited work has been made to investigate the possibility of combining conventional segmentation methods with the recently introduced deep learning semantic segmentation models to achieve effective outlining of the kidney. This study investigates the feasibility of combining deep learning semantic segmentation with a conventional active contour segmentation algorithm with the goal of improving the outlining of the kidney in ultrasound images. In particular, the performance of three deep learning semantic segmentation models, which are configured to use different backbone convolutional neural networks, has been studied in terms of their ability to detect the pixels that belong to the kidney in the ultrasound image. The best performing semantic segmentation approach is used to generate an initial outline for the kidney. Furthermore, a conventional edge-based active contour segmentation algorithm is used to refine and improve the initial kidney outline. The results indicate that our proposed approach for combining the deep learning semantic segmentation with the conventional edge-based active contour segmentation has achieved effective kidney outlining with Precision, Recall, F1-score, Accuracy, and Jaccard values of 94.2%, 89.6%, 91.0%, 98.4%, and 84.5%, respectively.

articleTitle: Sparse Recovery for ISAR Imaging via Nuclear Norm Minimization
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Missing entries of the backscattered data matrix deteriorate the quality of the resulting ISAR images. In this paper a data recovery method based on nuclear norm minimization (NNM) to recover the missing samples is proposed. Real and imaginary parts of the data are completed separately and a higher quality ISAR image is obtained by the 2D Fourier trans-form of the recovered matrix. The method has been compared to inexact augmented Lagrangian multipliers (IALM) and 2D smoothed LO (2D-SLO) methods both visually and quantitatively under three missing scenarios for two different missing ratios. The performance improvement is handled for both quantitative metrics such as root mean square error (RMSE) and correlation. For proposed method, RMSE scores difference can be higher than % 50 for the some extreme cases, whereas improvements in the correlation scores generally vary between %5-%10 when compared to the other methods.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of a Nanogrid Considering Communication Delay Time
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The decommissioning of conventional power plants, the rise of the installation of inverter-based technology for the supply of electrical energy in the distribution network as well as the application of information and communication technologies (ICT) bring new questions to the system stability in power systems. In addition to this, inverter-based technology should be able to provide ancillary services as conventional power plants do, such as active and reactive power provision for frequency and voltage control, respectively. Moreover, nanogrids or households are not only equipped nowadays with inverter-based technology, but also capable of providing these ancillary services. This research work presents a systematic approach for analyzing the stability of a nanogrid considering communication delay time. As noted in this scientific work, the higher the communication delay, the higher is the approximation of the poles to the origin, which influences the stability of the system.

articleTitle: Students' Satisfaction towards Blackboard: An Integration of Technology Acceptance Model for Quality eLearning
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In the current era of digital transformation, the COVID-19 pandemic has prompted the rapid adoption of new technologies in education. eLearning platforms, such as Blackboard, have been widely used by educators as a means of delivering instruction. In order to maximize student satisfaction and motivation in online learning, it is important to carefully consider the selection and use of high-quality tools. This study employs a quantitative method, using a questionnaire administered via Google Forms, to investigate students' satisfaction with Blackboard through the lens of technology acceptance model (TAM). The sample for this study consists of 146 students from private higher education institutions. The findings indicate that students hold positive perceptions of the system quality, service quality, quality of life, and behavioural intention to use Blackboard. This study thus supports the conclusion that Blackboard is an effective and suitable platform for online teaching and learning, as reflected in its quality aspects as measured by TAM.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Diagnosis of Major Depressive Disorder Using Electroencephalography Signals
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Not only is early diagnosis of Depression a critical issue as it is a fast-growing disease in this current decade, but also collecting data from this group of patients is very challenging as they cannot be relaxing and stay still. In this study, we aimed to use a limited number of Electroencephalography (EEG) electrodes to make it easier for the clinician and patient and develop a Conventional Neural Network (CNN) model to help the clinician to have a more accurate diagnosis of the disease. For this aim, we used two public EEG data of people with Major Depressive Disorder (MDD). Totally, the EEG data of 91 subjects (38 healthy and 53 MDD) were utilized in our study. After preprocessing, the spectrogram of EEG was used as input for the CNN model which was Mobile Net V2. The highest validation accuracy we could get was 91 % with a learning rate and batch size of 0.0001 and 32, respectively. Our results demonstrate that Mobile NET may have a high performance in MDD diagnosis.

articleTitle: Robust Controller Design for Time Delay Systems with Varying Parameters
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive study is presented on the problem of designing a robust controller for time delay systems with varying parameters by using H-infinity static output feedback. The motivation for this work is the need for a control strategy that can handle both external disturbances, uncertainties and time-varying delays in linear parameter varying (LPV) systems which have wide applications in various fields. A novel synthesis method is proposed based on a quadratic Lyapunov-Krasovskii functional which is used to derive a sufficient matrix inequality condition via a Jensen-type integral inequality. We introduce an iterative algorithm to efficiently search for a feasible solution set for the synthesis problem. In addition to the proposed synthesis method, a comprehensive review of existing literature on robust control for LPV systems with time-varying delays is also provided. Various techniques are compared and contrasted and their advantages and limitations are highlighted. Therefore, the readers are equipped with a balanced view of the state-of-the-art in this field such that our proposed method is put into context. To demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed approach, a numerical example is presented, along with comparison analysis. The results show that our method outperforms existing methods in terms of both stability and performance. Overall, this work offers a valuable contribution to the field of control engineering with potential applications in a variety of industries.

articleTitle: A Single Layer Miniaturized Band Stop Frequency Selective Surface with Oblique Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this paper, a highly compact single-layer frequency selective surface (FSS) with improved oblique stability is proposed for GSM shielding. The FSS element consists of interconnected concentric squares in each quadrant. These are connected with each other through outer convoluted square. The perimeter of the closed loop is significantly enhanced to lower the resonating frequency. This configuration successfully realizes the miniaturized FSS with band stop response. The unit cell size of FSS is reduced to 0.036 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_{0}\mathrm{x} 0.036 \lambda_{0}$</tex> at resonating frequency of 900 MHz. The elements of unit cells are placed in C4 rotational symmetry to provide the polarization independence. The proposed miniaturized FSS enables the angular insensitivity for both the transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarization. The FSS exhibits stable response, with no variation in resonating frequency for up to 83° of incident angle variation. The other salient features of this FSS are simple geometry and low thickness. The resonating phenomenon of the FSS is explained with the help of distribution of current and electric field.

articleTitle: Detection of Skin Cancer Using Artificial Intelligent Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Early recognition of skin malignancy can possibly decrease mortality and morbidity. In this paper, image processing was used to detect the early stages of skin cancer. The images were classified into 12 features (mean, standard deviation, compactness index, skewness, kurtosis, color variation, asymmetry index, entropy, energy, contrast, correlation and homogeneity). In the second stage, artificial intelligent techniques like neural network (ANN) and adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) techniques utilized to detect if there is abnormal growth of cell on the skin or not. A small number of training samples, 74 randomly selected images from well documented literature, was enough to accurately predict abnormal growth of cell. The accuracy of ANN and ANFIS were 90.2% and 97.48 % respectively. The percentage error between the real data and the resulting data for ANN and ANFIS were 0.034876 and 0.03277 respectively. The result shows the effectiveness and robustness of these techniques.

articleTitle: Reliability and Availability Analysis for Electronic Circuit Design
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper provides a reliability, availability and Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) analysis for a sample DC/DC converter and Discrete I/O electronic circuit stages. These analyses were performed using the Failure Tree Analyses (FTA) approach. The reason for choosing these structures is that they are frequently used in today's electronic design. In this study, the effect of the importance of reliability on the whole system, starting from a component in electronic circuit design, has been demonstrated.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Power Devices for Bridgeless Totem-Pole PFC at Different Switching Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Bridgeless Totem-Pole power factor correction (BTPPFC) topology is very attractive compared to other power factor correction (PFC) topologies due to its simplicity and minimal components. However, BTPPFC could not gained enough popularity with traditional Silicon MOSFET (Si-MOSFET) due to efficiency issues. BTPPFC has hard-switching structure, so it introduces high turn-on loss. Especially reverse recovery loss reduces efficiency considerably. However, with the development of new generation switches such as silicon carbide MOSFET (SiC-MOSFET), Gallium Nitride (GaN) enhancement mode high electron mobility transistors (E-HEMT), Cascode GaN HEMT, BTPPFC topology has become available with high efficiency. This paper presents a performance analysis of Si-MOSFET, SiC-MOSFET, GaN E-HEMT and Cascode GaN HEMT in terms of efficiency for BTPPFC topology at different switching frequencies.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Smart “Baby NO CRY” Cradle
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: There has long been a demand for a brand-new, lower-priced electronic cradle that could rival the expensive, currently imported ones. Nevertheless, except for the price, there is a limitation in the existing studies of the electronic cradles since they have only one intensity of the swing and omit the lullaby. Gentle, and regular movements that imitate the motion they felt in the womb are soothing to infants. A fussy or restless baby may be more easily calmed and lulled to sleep in a cradle with a more substantial swing. The importance of adding music sounds with swinging is that it can influence the child's development. Hence, the research aims to create an electronic cradle that is able to alter swing intensity and lullaby sound regarding a baby's cry amplitude to calm the baby. This paper describes creating and designing a modern, inexpensive, and indigenous “Baby NO CRY” smart electronic cradle. First, the sound analyzing system detects the infant's cry, and the cradle starts swinging until the sound stops; second, in addition to the swinging, the lullaby is integrated to be played to calm the baby. According to the intensity of the voice, the cradle will swing at three speeds (high, medium, and low), and the loudness of the lullaby also has three volumes in conformity with the swing speeds. Thus, this intelligent cradle model calms the baby instantly and provides restful sleep, allowing parents to care for infants without any interaction while working on or doing some other things.

articleTitle: Analysis of Inductively Coupled Circuits in Terms of Stability Issues
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Analysis of the system stability is an important aspect in its correct design. Different stability analysis methods have been developed over time, especially in the field of control engineering and signal processing. In this work the stability criteria were adapted to analog electrical circuits with lumped parameters that include inductive coupling. Different aspects related to the stability of circuits with and without magnetic coupling were analyzed. A comparative study was also included; it followed the influence of the quality of the magnetic coupling on the aspects related to the stability of the system and its behavior in dynamic regimes.

articleTitle: MYbody: Augmented Reality Mobile App for Understanding Body Boundaries Using MADLC
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Child abuse is a major problem in our society. This topic has aroused the curiosity of modern society. As a result, teaching children about the interrelationship of body boundaries should begin at a young age. In this project, it is proposed to develop a mobile app for a picture book AR that uses augmented reality (AR) as an advanced technology. Virtual objects projected through a display device augment the view of the physical book. The mobile app AR used the Mobile App Development Lifecycle (MADLC) methodology throughout the development process. The AR technique is marker-based, where the user follows a provided marker to activate the AR storybook. The expected outcome of this project is to raise awareness among parents and children about child sexual abuse. In addition, teachers can use MYbody AR mobile apps in the classroom to teach children about body boundaries. Future work of MYbody AR mobile apps includes adding more scenes as examples and working with the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development to create additional content.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of Machine Learning Methods for Intrusion Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In this work, we applied 8 machine learning (ML) techniques to detect intrusions, namely, neural networks, kNN, SVM, random forest, trees, AdaBoost, naive Bayes, and stochastic gradient descent SGD. Using the NSL-KDD data set, these ML techniques were trained and tested to correctly classify the network and operating system records of this dataset into one of 24 possible attacks. The performances of these ML methods were analyzed and compared, with the random forest method performing at the top. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work on investigating more than 4 ML classifiers on this data set in one single work and using the same set of tools.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Vibrational Activity of Laminated Cases of Traction Electric Machines According to Actual Condition
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Vibration diagnostics is one of the effective tools for solving a wide range of problems of detecting defects in electrical machines, preventing failure of parts, extending the service life and increasing the overhaul periods of their operation. Simultaneously occurring electromagnetic and mechanical processes during operation significantly complicate the collection and analysis of vibration parameters due to the presence of a large number of harmonic and random components in the experimental data signal. Preservation of electrical safety, reliability and durability of the operation of electromechanical equipment of electric drives based on asynchronous motors in transport remains an urgent task of electrical systems. The determining factor in the effective functioning of diagnostic systems is the establishment of a one-to-one correspondence between the parameters of diagnostic features, determined from the results of current measurements of the machine characteristics, and the type of defects that have arisen. These can be design errors, violations of the technological process of production, maintenance and repair of electrical machines, as well as intensive non-repair operation, all this leads to various kinds of defects.

articleTitle: The Analysis of Charging EVs in Parking Lot with Mode-3 22 kW Charger Powered by Grid-Connected 1 MW Solar Power Plant Using PVsyst
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The usage of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has become much more common in recent years, with the reduction of fossil resources. Some countries are considering banning the sale of vehicles with internal combustion engines. As a result of increase in usage of EV, the consumption of electrical energy is increasing exponentially. If this energy demand can be met by renewable energy sources rather than fossil fuels in the future, then these restrictions for sale of combustion engine vehicles will make sense. In this study, charging of electric cars powered by a grid-connected solar power plant with IMW installed power in a workplace parking lot located in Ankara province of Turkey is discussed. In this design, 33 Mode-3 22kW electric charging stations are used and energy flows analyzed with PV syst software. The energy produced through solar systems, the energy consumed, the energy sold to the grid, and losses have been calculated. The results show that usage of the energy generated by solar energy systems for charging electric vehicles is much more profitable in economic terms compared to selling it to the grid traditionally. This approach and obtained results show that reduce the payback time of the proposed system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Smart Watch Textile Antenna for Wi-Fi Bio Medical Applications in Millimetric Wave Band
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper is devoted to the design and implementation of smart watch textile antenna for Wi-Fi bio-medical applications in millimetric wave bands. The antenna is implemented on the leather textile-based substrate to be embedded in a smart watch. It enables the watch to pick up Wi-Fi signals without the need to be connected to a mobile through Bluetooth. It operates at 60 GHz or WiGig (Wireless Gigabit Alliance) band with a wide band for higher-rate applications. It also could be implemented over many stratified layers of the body organisms to be used in the diagnosis of many diseases like diabetes and cancer. The structure is designed and simulated using CST (Studio Suite) program. The wearable patch antenna has an octagon shape and it is implemented on leather material that acted as a flexible substrate with a size of 5.632 x 6.4 x 2 mm <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, relative permittivity of 2.95, and loss tangent of 0.006. The feeding is carried out using differential feed (discrete port in CST). This work provides five antenna implementations; antenna without ground, a ground is added at the back of the antenna in order to increase the antenna gain, the substrate dimensions are increased to 15 x 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to resemble the real hand watch size, layers of skin and fat are added under the ground of the antenna to study the effect of human body tissues human on the antenna performance. Finally, the whole structure is bent. It is found that the antenna can achieve a simulated peak realized gain in dB of 5.68, 7.28, 6.15, 3.03, and 4.37 for antenna without ground, antenna with the ground, antenna with larger substrate dimensions, antenna with skin and fat, and bent structure, respectively. The antenna with ground exhibits high gain, while adding the human organisms absorption, the gain is degraded because of human absorption. The bent structure contributes to higher gain.

articleTitle: A Novel Secure Algorithmic Infrastructure for V2V Systems Using Switched Beam Antenna System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: V2V security is crucial in ensuring that the communication between vehicles is protected from unauthorized access and tampering, which can lead to safety issues and loss of trust in the technology. Switched beam antennas are a specific type of antenna that can change the direction of the beam they transmit or receive, in order to improve the communication performance and coverage in V2V as compared to omnidirectional antennas. However, they are more prone to cyber attacks due to multiple access points In this research, a secure environment for a switched beam antenna system in the V2V ecosystem using machine learning technology is proposed. Cyberattacks are externally injected, and the behavior is observed by incorporating the proposed technology. Overall, a significant increase in throughput is observed with strong V2V communication in dense environments over significant distances.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Power Flow Analysis of Power Systems with PV and Wind Using Monte Carlo Method
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: With the increase in renewable energy systems, the increasing uncertainties in power systems make the analysis with deterministic power flow method insufficient. Probabilistic load flow allows us to see the distribution of bus voltage, bus angles and power flowing in the lines according to variable production and consumption values. With these distributions, the probabilities of variables exceeding their limit values are found, and risk analysis is performed. There are two main methods in PPF studies: analytical and numerical. Since the numerical method is more accurate than analytical methods, we opt to use the numerical method. In this study, a probabilistic power flow tool is developed using Monte Carlo Simulation. Three main case studies are analyzed in this publication. The first one was done to verify the correctness of the system. In the second study, n-l contingency analysis was performed. In the third study, the existing generators are replaced with PV and their effects on the system are observed. In order to test the developed tool, a modified 9-bus and IEEE 14 bus test systems were used and compared with a previous study. The results showed that the tool was accurate and faster than the previous studies. This developed tool can also be used as a benchmark to further PPF studies.

articleTitle: Self-Adaptive Genetic Algorithm For Permutation Flow Shop Scheduling Problems
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The permutation flow shop scheduling problem (PFSSP) is a well-known, extensively researched, and heavily applied non-polynomial (NP)-Hard combinatorial optimization problem. It is encountered in various real-life manufacturing problems such as automotive manufacturing, integrated circuit fabrication, and agricultural food industries. It continues to gain popularity in operational research areas as new manufacturing areas are developed. Therefore, finding a solution to these NP-Hard problems attract the attention of scientists. In this paper, we studied a PFSSP and proposed a new heuristic for its solution: The Self-Adaptive Genetic Algorithm (GA). This proposed algorithm uses a conventional GA with cycle crossover and random swap mutation. Its novelty, on the other hand, lies in incorporating an adaptive mechanism in the GA. The proposed algorithm uses three different local searches (i.e. 2-Opt, Greedy Insert, and Greedy Swap local searches) based on their successes. In other words, the proposed algorithm evaluates the performance of each local search at each generational iteration and makes a decision on which one to use based on their previous performances. The more successful local searches increase their probability of selection and vice versa. This way, Self-Adaptive GA, hence the name, adapts and directs its exploitation by the information it obtains in its previous generations. The proposed algorithm was applied to a subset of well-known Taillard problem instances. The experimental studies show its successful performance. Self-Adaptive GA obtained the optimum results for 7 out of 18 benchmark instances. In the rest of the 11 instances, the differences between the results of the proposed method and the optimum values are less than 2%.

articleTitle: A Two-Tier Control Algorithm Based on XGBoost Model to Speed up Smart-Grids Management
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Since most of holistic centralized and decentralized methods do not address the problems related to speed in smart-grids, deep-learning and machine-learning methods can be employed outstanding ways to reinforce the stability of power systems with high speed and accuracy. This paper introduces a two-tier control algorithm based on a regression supervised-learning idea to meet both above-mentioned requirements in a group of smart-grids and inverter-based distributed power systems. In this, the power and load managements alongside the supervised learning idea are employed to rapidly detect correlations between real-power, voltage, and frequency. To prove the performance of the proposed algorithm, the modified standard IEEE 37-bus smart-grid is considered, where its steady-state and dynamic results indicate noteworthy effects of that.

articleTitle: Police Car Emergency Signaling System
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: A police car emergency system with modern elements has been developed and implemented, bringing innovation to the already existing commercially available beacons. The new features of the work are present both on the visual side, in the LED light displays with predefined texts to be shown, and on the audio side, in the sound messages of warning. Numerous electronic components have been used for practical implementation to bring the whole concept to life. LED matrix and power LEDs were successfully used to develop the visual part of the police system. The MP3 module and its related circuit led to the audio implementation of the proj ect. The audio control was achieved using a two-channel relay to connect signal wires from a horn microphone and the MP3 module. The entire system is controlled with Arduino N ano development boards.

articleTitle: A Broadband Frequency-to-Voltage Converter for Sinusoidal Signals Based on Filters Design
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The frequency-to-voltage converter is a versatile circuit that translates variations in frequency to a corresponding voltage level. However, converting high-frequency signals into a DC output voltage has been a challenging task. This paper proposes a new, yet simple, approach for converting the frequency into a DC output voltage of sinusoidal signals. The frequency-to-voltage conversion is achieved by utilizing the attenuation band of a filter. The paper provides a clear mathematical model and a relation between frequency and DC output voltage levels, with merely passive components for efficient power consumption. This technique is implemented to achieve wide frequency spectrum conversion that could extend to tens of MHz and beyond. The proposed scheme is verified experimentally in both low-frequency range, varying in sub-kilohertz, and as high as 40MHz.

articleTitle: Influence of Space Between the Lower and Upper Windings on the Leakage Reactance of the Split-Winding Transformer
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The higher current due to the short-circuit conditions in split-winding transformers can cause damage to the equipment. Due to this, it is important to analyze and study the effect of the different factors on leakage reactance. In this work, the three-dimensional finite element analysis is used to compute and evaluate the effect of the axial distance between two windings (lower and upper sides) of the split winding transformer on leakage reactance. A 3.15 MVA, 6.3/0.69 kV split-winding transformer is used as a prototype to investigate its leakage reactance under the different gaps between the lower and upper sides. The results reveal that the leakage reactance of the split winding transformers generally varies with the change in the distance between the upper winding and lower winding of the transformer. Moreover, there is a considerable difference between the leakage reactance during the different cases. In the case of the lower gap between the lower and upper sides, the leakage reactance is higher. On the other side, the leakage reactance is less during the higher gap between the upper and lower windings. A prototype is also manufactured with the suggested distance and the finite element method's accuracy is verified.

articleTitle: Development of Liquid Crystal Display Printed Antennas for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Liquid crystal display (LCD) printing technique has been widely used in developing various antenna devices. As the inherent dielectric properties of the resin, such as the permittivity, it may limit the option of practical solutions. To broaden the use of commercial UV resin in antenna designs, we propose an easy way to increase the permittivity of the original cured resin by adding the Al2O3 to the uncured liquid resin. Measurement results show that the modified permittivity of such a printable composite can be increased from 2.8 to 4.4 at 24 GHz. In terms of the antenna applications, we show four antenna designs, including horn, rod, and lens antennas fabricated by LCD printing and the modified resin. Simulation and measurement results confirm that the proposed method offers a good platform for bringing superior radiation performance together with low-cost fabrication compared with typical antennas.

articleTitle: Lightweight Authentication and Communication Protocol for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: At present, smart home based Internet of Things (IoT) technology has been developed and applied widely. Applications include automatic or remote control on-off electronics and electrical appliances in which users can send commands to a device gateway or an IoT device via smart devices. During the past few years, many research papers have investigated security and authentication protocols for IoT devices. However, they are still lack of consideration for the power constraints of IoT devices. This work presents a security and authentication protocol which reduces the use of hash functions and encryption method. Therefore, it consumes less power during the communication operation and, hence, complies with the power limitation of IoT and mobile devices.

articleTitle: Generation and Spectrum Analysis of C Band ASE Using Erbium-Doped Fibers with Different Properties
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: In C band light source generating, self-amplified emission (Amplified spontaneous Emission - ASE) is usually used. For this, erbium-doped fiber amplifiers (EDFA) are operated without an input signal. In this paper, 3 different EDFA setups and 7 different erbium-doped fibers in each of these setups generated ASE along the C band. The real factory parameters of the erbium-doped fibers (EDFs) used in these setups used in the simulation environment were created as data files and the accuracy of the simulation was increased. After the setups were simulated, the average output power and ripple values were optimized along the C band and the EDF, and the setup that gave the best spectrum was determined.

articleTitle: The Optimal Parameters Matching of Hybrid Energy Storage System for Battery Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: It is the consensus of the world that mass penetration of battery electric vehicles (BEVs) is the main solution to urban air pollution. At present, the battery electric vehicles use lithium ion battery as energy storage system. However, the current performance of energy, power and durability for lithium battery still cannot fully meet the requirement of all utility of BEVs, especially in the high charging and discharging rate conditions, which will bring the negative impact on battery performance. The super-capacitor exhibits an excellent high charging, therefore, the hybrid energy storage compose of lithium battery and super-capacitor combines the advantage of lithium battery and super-capacitor to make it has great potential for high power charging for BEV. However, the BEV with hybrid energy storage system could exhibit excellent only when the components of it was well designed. Therefore, this paper t focuses the method of optimal component sizing for the energy storage system for battery electric bus of 12 meters length. We propose the optimal component sizing scheme targeting minimization of the life cycle cost of BEV, considering different daily traveled vehicle kilometers and driving cycles. The cost model based on the battery degradation model is set up, and the global optimization algorithm is used to obtain the optimal power split ratio to obtain operating cost. The results show that the proposed method can economically operate and optimal designed hybrid energy storage system provide important basis for the optimal control strategy.

articleTitle: SIGW Based Array of Hexagonal Slot Antennas for Sub-6 Cellular LTE/5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This article is devoted to design, analysis and fabrication of an array of hexagonal slot antennas fed through Substrate Integrated Gap Waveguide (SIGW) divider configuration. The structure provides low dispersion, low loss antenna with high gain. Two dielectric material are used for implementation, Roger RO 4350c is used for the bottom layer of the SIGW structure. This layer includes the divider of branched ridge structure surrounded with periodic vias to confine the wave propagation over the ridge. The second layer is the top one, includes the top ground in which the slot antennas are etched. The structure is analyzed using the Finite Deference Time Domain (FDTM) analysis (CST microwave studio). It provides a triple band for Sub-6 Cellular LTE/5G Applications. It operates at 5.9, 6 and 6.1414 GHz with reasonable gain. It is fabricated using PCB technology and measured using vector network analyzer which finding reasonable agreement between the measured and simulated reflection coefficients. The antenna achieves a reasonable gain for the adopted applications.

articleTitle: An Eco-Friendly Smartphone-Charging Locker with a Solar Panel and Multi-Factor Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: The need to be constantly connected to the internet while being outside has become the new norm. As a result, people cannot afford to have a dead phone battery in the middle of the day. This project aims to solve the dead phone battery problem by proposing charging lockers using solar panels to charge the smartphones. The system consists of a wooden locker, solar panel, a solenoid lock, Arduino microcontroller, keypad as well as a fingerprint scanner. Controlled by the C-programmed Arduino microcontroller, the system utilizes solar energy to charge smartphones and offers a secure lock that is controlled by input from a keypad, and a fingerprint scanner.

articleTitle: Detecting the Regions-of-Interest that Enclose the Tumors in Breast Ultrasound Images Using the RetinaNet Model
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Ultrasound imaging provides an effective modality to diagnose breast cancer, but the task of interpreting breast ultrasound images is complex and challenging. Computer-aided diagnosis systems can enhance the accuracy of ultrasound-based breast cancer diagnosis, but the creation of these systems necessitates the utilization of effective techniques for detecting the region-of-interest (ROI) that encloses the tumor. The goal of our study is to investigate the effectiveness of utilizing the RetinaNet deep learning model for detecting the ROIs in breast ultrasound images. To the best of our knowledge, the RetinaNet model has not been employed previously to detect the ROIs in breast ultrasound images. To achieve this goal, the ultrasound image is processed using contrast enhancement and sharpening to synthesize an RGB image with the aim of improving the possibility of detecting the ROI. The synthesized RGB image is analyzed using a fine-tuned RetinaNet model to detect the ROI. The performance of the RetinaNet model was assessed and compared with four leading deep learning object detection models, using a dataset of 380 breast ultrasound images. The results demonstrate that the RetinaNet model outperformed the other models, with a failure rate of 7%, a mean recall value of 89%, a mean precision value of 89%, and a mean F1-score value of 88%. These findings suggest that the RetinaNet model provides a feasible and effective approach for detecting the ROIs in breast ultrasound images.

articleTitle: Optimizing Fused Deposition Modeling with ANN: Material Consumption and Tensile Strength Predictions
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: Conventional modelling was once favored for process modelling for its straightforward nature and simplicity. However, conventional modelling is incapable of modelling complex processes such as fused deposition modelling (FDM). This study aims to model an accurate FDM process using an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict material consumption and tensile strength based on layer height, infill density, printing temperature and printing speed. The design of the experiment (DOE) was constructed using face-centered central composite design (FCCCD) yielding a total of 78 specimens. The material consumption was measured by weighting the specimen using a densimeter while the tensile strength of the specimen was tested using a universal testing machine (UTM). Best ANN structures were first identified in a trained network before being modelled for comparison. Models were compared using the lowest mean squared error (MSE), root mean squared error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and highest coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). The best predictive model structure for material consumption is 4-19-14-1 with the lowest MSE of 0.00096 while the best predictive model structure for tensile strength is 4-16-15-12-1 with the lowest MSE of 0.005274145.

articleTitle: Measurement of Trash Percentage for Mechanical Harvested Sugarcane Using Multispectral Image
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This research aimed to develop a new technique for estimating the percentage of trash in mechanically harvested sugarcane samples using multispectral imaging and machine learning. The research found that the Random Forest model with a Classification Tree of 150 was the most effective classification model, with a Quality Percentage of 96.05%. In addition, the best prediction models for estimating the weight of sugarcane billet using Multiple Linear Regression had an R2 value of 0.77 and a Root Mean Square Error of calibration (RMSEC) value of 21.03 g. The results of the research also showed that the new technique was capable of accurately estimating the percentage of trash in sugarcane samples, with a Root Mean Square Error of prediction (RMSEP) of 2.09% when compared to traditional methods. This suggests that the new technique may be a useful, rapid method for assessing the percent of sugarcane billet and trash in production processes.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Textile-Based Perfect Superstrate Metamaterial Absorber for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 10th International Conference on Electrical and Electronics Engineering (ICEEE)
abstract: This paper presents an ultra-wideband textile-based perfect Metamaterial absorber for 6G applications. The design geometry of the unit cell is based on a modified split ring resonator and optimized akin to the word 6G. It enables a wideband in sub-THz at the standard of FCC.
